differentiation.occupancy_preservation: The usage-balancing component adjusts codewords through their soft-assignment probabilities, while the centroid barrier repels codewords from an overly tight centroid geometry. The directed KL component penalizes source and target assignment distributions that become indistinguishable. These terms do not minimize the distance between a transition's two codewords; the KL term instead favors different endpoint distributions. A zero barrier gradient can occur when the separation threshold is already met.

vs_r8.why: Unlike encoder-only auxiliary losses, this objective has an explicit codebook gradient. Unlike pairwise curvature or directed code-assignment cross-entropy that can pull endpoint codewords together, it includes a codeword-spread barrier and a directed assignment-divergence term that penalizes shared endpoint distributions. It targets balanced soft usage rather than rewarding code merging, though its hard-export behavior must still be verified.

differentiation.vs_reference_arm: the reference arm is the untouched host; this candidate adds one term whose gradient reaches the codebook without pulling a transition's two codewords together

equation: For each valid pair, let p_s(c)=softmax_c(-||source-codebook_c||^2/tau) and p_t(c)=softmax_c(-||target-codebook_c||^2/tau). Let u_c be the masked, batch-mean of p_s(c)+p_t(c), and let q_c=1/C. Let d_c=||codebook_c-mean_j(codebook_j)||^2. L=weight*(sum_c (u_c-q_c)^2 + separation_weight*sum_c q_c*relu(min_separation-d_c)^2 + direction_weight*mean_b KL(p_s||p_t)).
expected_failure_modes: Uniform soft usage and a centroid-spread barrier may preserve code usage without preserving useful item distinctions; the directed KL can also over-separate common transitions. The soft objective may not translate into hard assignment changes, and the frozen run could therefore fail to improve Stage-3 retrieval despite healthy soft statistics.

forbidden_substitutions.reason: a quota on the assignment is the family that produced 39.5% and 24.2% occupancy without preserving the exported codes
a term that pulls a pair's two codewords together is what collapsed the level-0 codebook to two codes

hypotheses: Reject if the cold run's exported level-0 Gini exceeds the control's 0.216, L1-to-L2 branches fall below 65.91 per L1 code, train-to-test frequency drift grows, sequence information falls, or the single held-out Stage-3 recall@10 does not exceed 0.06406796775709883.

symbols.KL(p_s||p_t): Kullback-Leibler divergence from source assignment distribution to target assignment distribution.
symbols.d_c: Squared distance of codeword c from the codebook centroid.
symbols.direction_weight: Coefficient on the directed source-to-target assignment divergence.
symbols.mask: Valid-pair indicator, shape [B]; only valid pairs contribute to batch means.
symbols.min_separation: Minimum desired squared distance from a codeword to the codebook centroid.
symbols.p_s(c): Soft source-to-codeword assignment probability for codeword c.
symbols.p_t(c): Soft target-to-codeword assignment probability for codeword c.
symbols.separation_weight: Coefficient on the codeword-centroid separation barrier.
symbols.target: Target item representation, shape [B,D]; its distinct role makes the transition directed.
symbols.u_c: Masked mean soft usage of codeword c across source and target endpoints.
symbols.weight: Overall coefficient multiplying this auxiliary loss.
